g1-implement.title: Refuse tierless dispatch; forward reasoning_effort as --effort
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for this gate, per the converged plan in PLAN_CONVERGENCE.md (read it first -- it resolves several sub-decisions below, do not re-derive them). Refusal seam: add ONE guard clause to CrewSpec.__post_init__ (scripts/run_crew.py:1350-1364, alongside its two existing invariant checks, same style, same CrewLaunchError/exit-1/REFUSED: shape) refusing a falsy self.model, fail closed, no invented default (decision:refuse-a-tierless-dispatch). Do NOT put the check in build_crew_argv or make --model required=True at the argparse layer (build_parser) -- both were independently rejected by both plan candidates: --resume and a bare --abandon legitimately pass no --model and must stay legal at the parser layer, and --resume/CliBackend.resume never construct a CrewSpec at all (it reads entry.get("model") off the registry dict), so the seam already exempts it by construction. RULED (do not re-litigate): --abandon --relaunch requires an explicit --model with NO fallback to abandoned.get("model") -- this is intentionally asymmetric with reasoning_effort's existing inherit-on-relaunch fallback (main() line ~2071, args.reasoning_effort or abandoned.get(...)), which stays untouched (decision:do-not-change-what-anything-runs-at). Add a test proving the refusal fires before CliBackend.dispatch reserves scratch/writes the running registry entry (issue #525 ordering) -- assert no half-written entry results from a refused fresh launch. Effort wiring: add `effort: str | None = None` to build_crew_argv, `if effort: argv += ["--effort", effort]` mirroring the existing model line (813-814); thread `effort=spec.reasoning_effort` from CliBackend.dispatch (~1542) and `effort=entry.get("reasoning_effort")` from CliBackend.resume (~1612) -- both call sites, a resume that silently drops effort reproduces the exact defect this mission fixes. Confirm build_entry's existing `if model: entry["model"] = model` / `if reasoning_effort: entry["reasoning_effort"] = reasoning_effort` already satisfies decision:record-the-resolved-tier and decision:reasoning-effort-follows-tier's recording half once model is mandatory -- pin with a test, do not re-implement. Flip the pre-mission-contract tests that currently assert `assertNotIn("--reasoning-effort", ...)` (test_reasoning_effort_is_metadata_only_and_recorded ~2588, test_cli_resume_reads_reasoning_effort_from_registry ~2605, test_legacy_resume_without_reasoning_effort_does_not_crash ~2623, test_abandon_relaunch_inherits_stored_reasoning_effort_when_not_reasserted ~955) to assert `--effort <value>` IS present when reasoning_effort is set (both dispatch and resume) and absent when it is not (including the legacy-entry-with-no-field case) -- correct their docstrings, they currently describe the pre-mission contract as a guarantee. Add test_crewspec_refuses_missing_model and a green companion test_crewspec_accepts_explicit_model (pure CrewSpec construction, no main()/argparse/subprocess). Add a registry-entry-direct assertion test (dispatch with both model+reasoning_effort set, assert on entry["model"]/entry["reasoning_effort"] directly, not via argv) covering both fresh dispatch and the relaunch path's NEW attempt entry. Caller-list survey (deliverable, not optional): after the refusal lands, run the full suite once, enumerate every failure whose message contains the refusal text, classify each as (a) a test in tests/test_crew_launcher.py needing an explicit model= -- fix directly, this file is owned -- or (b) a caller outside owned files -- report, do not fix. Report the full list verbatim in IMPLEMENTER_RESULT even if empty (both plan candidates' independent greps found zero non-test-file callers, but re-verify, don't trust the candidates). Two of the four flip-tests (at least test_cli_resume_reads_reasoning_effort_from_registry ~2605) construct CrewSpec(...) with no model= at all -- once the refusal lands they need an explicit model= added directly, in the SAME edit as their --effort assertion flip, not left for the later caller-list survey to independently rediscover. THE TRAP: when you (the Commander) dispatch this gate's own implementer crew via run_crew.py, pass --model explicitly (this run's tier, sonnet) -- this is the mission's own named trap (naming a tier for every crew dispatched, from the first dispatch, before the refusal you're building makes it mandatory). Anchors below.
